Fibroblast foci. Discrete bulges of immature fibroblasts in amphophilic matrix are referred to as fibroblast or fibroblastic foci. They occur at the interface between dense scar and adjacent normal lung. In a three-dimensional reconstruction study, the foci appear to be interconnected into a lattice. These lesions are thought to be the focus of ongoing injury and repair in usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP), but are not unique to UIP. H&E stain, 200xoriginal magnification.

full.description: This is a high-power photomicrograph of lung tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The image displays characteristic patchy interstitial fibrosis with dense scar formation interspersed with active fibroblastic foci. These discrete aggregates of immature fibroblasts and myofibroblasts are located at the interface between dense fibrosis and relatively normal lung parenchyma. These histological findings are classic and most characteristic of usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP).

random.description: This is a histopathological micrograph of lung tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin. The image displays intra-alveolar fibroblastic plugs, also known as Masson bodies, within the alveolar ducts and spaces. These findings are characteristic of organizing pneumonia, such as cryptogenic organizing pneumonia (COP) or bronchiolitis obliterans organizing pneumonia (BOOP). The surrounding alveolar architecture remains relatively preserved with mild chronic interstitial inflammation.
